en.title: Spain: immigration-led scale, renewable power and the productivity test behind Europe's growth outlier
en.deck: Spain is outperforming large euro-area peers through employment, immigration, tourism and investment, but weak productivity, double-digit housing inflation and future ageing determine whether rapid aggregate growth becomes durable convergence in income per person.
en.regime: Fast-growing euro-area economy powered by labour-force expansion, migration, tourism and renewable investment, with the next phase dependent on productivity, housing supply and post-recovery-fund capital formation.
en.key_risk: Growth remains labour-input intensive while housing and infrastructure lag population, causing real-income convergence to stall before ageing and fiscal pressures intensify.

pt-BR.title: Espanha: escala impulsionada por imigração, eletricidade renovável e o teste de produtividade por trás do crescimento europeu
pt-BR.deck: A Espanha supera grandes pares da área do euro por emprego, imigração, turismo e investimento, mas produtividade fraca, inflação imobiliária de dois dígitos e envelhecimento futuro determinam se o rápido crescimento agregado vira convergência durável da renda por habitante.
pt-BR.regime: Economia de rápido crescimento na área do euro, impulsionada por expansão da força de trabalho, migração, turismo e investimento renovável, cuja próxima fase depende de produtividade, oferta habitacional e formação de capital após os recursos de recuperação.
pt-BR.key_risk: O crescimento permanece intensivo em quantidade de trabalho enquanto moradia e infraestrutura ficam atrás da população, interrompendo a convergência da renda real antes da intensificação do envelhecimento e das pressões fiscais.

selection_rationale: Spain is one of the largest EU and NATO economies and is currently an outlier in European growth, labour-force expansion, tourism and renewable penetration, yet the public corpus lacks reusable country context. Existing research on European security, France and Germany requires a Spanish dossier to analyse southern-European growth, defence burden-sharing, energy interconnection, migration, housing capacity and the RRF transition without reconstructing these mechanisms repeatedly.
contrary_evidence: Spain's rapid GDP, employment and population growth supports a strong-convergence thesis, but productivity per hour remains weak and unemployment is still high relative to northern European peers.
Record tourism and visitor spending can be read as external strength, but housing, water and infrastructure pressures create local capacity costs that are not visible in export receipts.

Renewables already dominate electricity generation and create a potential industrial advantage, while grid, storage and limited French interconnection constrain how much additional capacity can be economically absorbed.
Housing prices are rising at double-digit rates, but stronger bank balance sheets and lower private leverage mean the current cycle does not yet reproduce the pre-2008 credit mechanism.
limitations: Quarterly GDP, employment and productivity observations can be revised; revised September 2026 national-accounts data are preferred over the July advance release.
The Spanish Recovery and Resilience Plan was materially revised; the updated 2026 European Commission envelope is not comparable with older headline amounts without reconciliation.
Housing prices do not directly measure affordability because wages, rents, mortgage rates and household formation also matter.
Renewable installed capacity, generation and self-consumption are distinct measures and must not be used interchangeably.
Defence spending is subject to differing political and accounting interpretations; capability claims and spending ratios are kept separate.
National water-storage percentages conceal severe regional and seasonal differences among river basins.
